Fits, cuts and filter optimization

The reports of LegendSpecFits are drawn by lplot: the fit of a distribution, the cuts derived from it, and the scans of the DSP filter optimization.

using CairoMakie, LegendMakie
using LegendSpecFits, Measurements, Unitful
using TypedTables, PropDicts

Truncated Gaussian fit

The fit of a truncated Gaussian to values, with the residuals of the fit.

x = 2.0 .+ 0.5 .* randn(10_000)
result, report = fit_single_trunc_gauss(x, (low = 0.0, high = 4.0, max = NaN))
lplot(report, xlabel = "x", title = "Truncated Gaussian fit")

Window cuts

A centered window cut keeps the values within a number of standard deviations of a half Gaussian fit to one side of a distribution centered at a known value, zero by default; the cut is drawn on the histogram.

slope = 0.5 .* randn(10_000)
result, report = get_centered_gaussian_window_cut(slope, -4.0, 4.0, 3.0, n_bins = -1)
lplot(report, xlabel = "Baseline slope", title = "Window cut")

The quality cuts of several parameters of a table are fit at once; the report holds one panel per parameter.

t = Table(baseline_slope = randn(100_000), baseline_std = 3.0 .+ randn(100_000))
config = PropDict(
    :baseline_slope => PropDict(:min => -10.0, :max => 10.0, :sigma => 2.0,
        :kwargs => PropDict(:relative_cut => 0.01, :n_bins => -1, :fixed_center => false, :left => false)),
    :baseline_std => PropDict(:min => -10.0, :max => 20.0, :sigma => 2.0,
        :kwargs => PropDict(:relative_cut => 0.01, :n_bins => -1, :fixed_center => false, :left => true)),
)
result, report = qc_window_cut(t, config)
lplot(report, figsize = (600, 700), title = "Quality cuts")

Filter optimization

The scans of a filter parameter are reported as a grid and the figure of merit at each point, with the minimum marked. The noise as a function of the rise time of the trapezoidal filter:

enc_grid_rt = (1.5:0.5:16.0)u"μs"
enc = measurement.(1.0 .+ 0.02 .* (ustrip.(enc_grid_rt) .- 8).^2 .+ 0.1 .* rand(length(enc_grid_rt)), 0.05)
min_enc, idx = findmin(enc)
rt = measurement(enc_grid_rt[idx], step(enc_grid_rt))
lplot((; rt, min_enc, enc_grid_rt, enc), title = "ENC noise")

The energy resolution, the W90 width, the asymmetry and the qdrift slope as a function of the flat-top time, with the optimum of the objective and the legacy FWHM optimum marked. An objective other than the FWHM, W90 or asymmetry is overlaid on the FWHM panel. The vectors hold the successful grid points, the table all of them:

e_grid_ft = collect((0.5:0.25:5.0)u"μs")
ok = [i != 4 for i in eachindex(e_grid_ft)]
fwhm_all = (2.5 .+ 0.3 .* (ustrip.(e_grid_ft) .- 2.5).^2 .+ 0.1 .* rand(length(e_grid_ft)))u"keV"
fwhm_all[.!ok] .= NaN * u"keV"
w90_all = 1.9 .* fwhm_all
asym_all = 1.0 .+ 0.05 .* rand(length(e_grid_ft))
fct_all = 1e-3 .* rand(length(e_grid_ft))
ct_spread_all = (0.4 .* rand(length(e_grid_ft)))u"keV"
objective_all = sqrt.(fwhm_all .^ 2 .+ (0.1 .* ct_spread_all) .^ 2)
table_ft = Table(ft = e_grid_ft, status = [o ? "ok" : "fit failed" for o in ok], fwhm = fwhm_all, w90 = w90_all,
    asym = asym_all, fct = fct_all, ct_spread = ct_spread_all)
i_best = argmin(i -> ok[i] ? ustrip(objective_all[i]) : Inf, eachindex(e_grid_ft))
report_ft = (
    ft = measurement(e_grid_ft[i_best], 0.25u"μs"), min_fwhm = fwhm_all[i_best], min_objective = objective_all[i_best],
    objective = :fwhm_ct, legacy_ft = measurement(e_grid_ft[i_best - 1], 0.25u"μs"),
    e_grid_ft = e_grid_ft[ok], fwhm = fwhm_all[ok], w90 = w90_all[ok], asym = asym_all[ok], fct = fct_all[ok],
    ct_spread = ct_spread_all[ok], objective_values = objective_all[ok], table = table_ft
)
lplot(report_ft, title = "Flat-top time scan")

The survival fraction of the single-escape peak as a function of the window length of the Savitzky-Golay filter of the current:

a_grid_wl_sg = (30:32.0:350)u"ns"
sfs = measurement.(10 .+ 0.001 .* (ustrip.(a_grid_wl_sg) .- 150).^2 .+ rand(length(a_grid_wl_sg)), NaN) .* u"percent"
min_sf, idx = findmin(sfs)
wl = measurement(a_grid_wl_sg[idx], step(a_grid_wl_sg))
lplot((; wl, min_sf, a_grid_wl_sg, sfs), title = "A/E filter")

The objective of the SiPM filter optimization as a function of the window length:

a_grid_wl_sg = (1.5:0.5:16.0)u"μs"
obj = measurement.(0.5 .+ 0.01 .* (ustrip.(a_grid_wl_sg) .- 6).^2 .+ 0.05 .* rand(length(a_grid_wl_sg)), 0.03)
min_obj, idx = findmin(obj)
wl = measurement(a_grid_wl_sg[idx], step(a_grid_wl_sg))
lplot((; wl, min_obj, gain = missing, res_1pe = missing, pos_1pe = missing, threshold = missing,
    a_grid_wl_sg, obj, report_simple = missing, report_fit = missing), title = "SiPM filter")

Residuals

The residual panels of the fit plots are drawn by residualplot!: the normalized residuals with the bands of one and three standard deviations.

fig = Figure(size = (600, 200))
ax = Axis(fig[1, 1], xlabel = "x", ylabel = "Residuals (σ)")
LegendMakie.residualplot!(ax, (x = 1:50, residuals_norm = randn(50)))
fig
